words: ذَٰلِكَ مِنْ أَنۢبَآءِ ٱلْغَيْبِ نُوحِيهِ إِلَيْكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tells Muhammad that the account of Zechariah, John, and Mary is unseen news revealed to him, although he was not present when they cast lots over Mary's care.
rows.anchor: يقول الله لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم {ذلك من أنباء الغيب نوحيه إليك} يعني بالخبر {الغيب} في قصة زكريا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He glosses al-ghayb here as the report concerning Zechariah, John, and Mary.
rows.anchor: يعني بالخبر {الغيب} في قصة زكريا ويحيى ومريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains the phrase as meaning that Muhammad was not among them or at their side.
rows.anchor: {وما كنت لديهم} يعني عندهم {إذ يلقون أقلامهم}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus is honored and established with God in this world and among those brought near in the next life.
rows.anchor: وجيها في الدنيا} يعني مكينا عند الله في الدنيا من المقربين في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He glosses al-mahd as al-khuraq, the term given in the source.
rows.anchor: {ويكلم الناس في المهد} يعني في الخرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus would speak to people as an adult when he returned before being raised to heaven.
rows.anchor: {وكهلا} ويكلمهم كهلا إذا اجتمع قبل أن يرفع إلى السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He identifies those described as righteous as the messengers.
rows.anchor: {ومن الصالحين} يعني من المرسلين

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb says Mary's fellow consecrated servant was her cousin Joseph, who served and spoke with her from behind the veil; he first noticed her pregnancy and was troubled, not knowing its cause.
rows.anchor: وأخرج اسحق بن بشر وابن عساكر عن وهب قال: لما استقر حمل مريم وبشرها جبريل وثقت بكرامة الله

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb recounts that Mary and Joseph fetched water together and returned to the church while angels brought Mary the glad tidings that God had chosen and purified her; Joseph wondered at what he heard.
rows.anchor: وكانت مريم إذا نفذ ماؤها وماء يوسف أخذا قلتيهما ثم انطلقا إلى المفازة التي فيها الماء

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: When Mary's pregnancy became evident, Joseph recalled her purification, her mother's prayer, the angels' words, Zechariah's protection, and the absence of Satan; seeing her changing color and swelling, he asked whether conception could occur without seed, and she said yes.
rows.anchor: فلما استبان ليوسف حمل مريم وقع في نفسه من أمرها حتى كاد أن يفتتن

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr reads لما with a doubled consonant in the phrase.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير أنه قرأ {لما آتيتكم} ثقل لما

rows.speaker: عاصم
rows.claim: Asim reads لما lightly and آتيتكم with one ت, understanding it as I gave you.
rows.anchor: عن عاصم أنه قرأ {لما} مخففة {آتيتكم} بالتاء على واحدة يعني أعطيتكم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses isri as my covenant.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {إصري} قال: عهدي

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali explains the command to witness as bearing witness concerning the communities and the covenant made with them.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن علي بن أبي طالب في قوله {قال فاشهدوا} يقول: فاشهدوا على أممكم

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali says whoever turns away from Muhammad after this covenant with all communities are sinners through disbelief.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن علي بن أبي طالب في قوله {قال فاشهدوا} يقول: فاشهدوا

words: وَلَهُۥٓ أَسْلَمَ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ طَوْعًۭا وَكَرْهًۭا
rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report with a weak chain says those in heaven are angels, those on earth include people born Muslim, and the coerced are captives of nations led to Paradise in chains despite their reluctance.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Anas reports the Prophet explaining that angels obey God in heaven and the Ansar and Abd al-Qays obey him on earth.
rows.anchor: وأخرج الديلمي عن أنس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says this submission occurred when God took the primordial covenant.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير من طريق مجاهد عن ابن عباس {وله أسلم من في السماوات والأرض طوعا وكرها} قال: حين أخذ الميثاق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains submission as their collective worship of God and links the wording to the verse about all in heaven and earth prostrating willingly or unwillingly.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم من طريق علي عن ابن عباس في الآية قال: عبادتهم لي أجمعين

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima calls this phrase separate, then restates the wording about those in heaven and earth submitting willingly or unwillingly.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم من طريق عكرمة عن ابن عباس {وله أسلم من في السماوات} قال: هذه مفصولة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses aslama as recognition or knowledge.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم من طريق سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس {وله أسلم} قال: المعرفة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid compares their submission to people's acknowledgment that God created the heavens and earth; that acknowledgment itself is their submission.
rows.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن جرير عن مجاهد في الآية قال: هو كقوله (ولئن سألتهم من خلق السموات والأرض ليقولن الله)

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-Aliya says every human acknowledged God as Lord and himself as God's servant: the polytheist submits unwillingly, while one who devotes worship to God submits willingly.
rows.anchor: عن أبي العالية في الآية قال: كل آدمي أقر

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says some peoples were compelled to accept Islam while others came to it willingly.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن الحسن في الآية قال: أكره أقوام على الإسلام وجاء أقوام طائعين

rows.speaker: مطر الوراق
rows.claim: Matar al-Warraq counts angels, the Ansar, Banu Sulaym, and Abd al-Qays as willing submitters, and everyone else as submitting unwillingly.
rows.anchor: وأخرج عن مطر الوراق في الآية قال: الملائكة طوعا والأنصار طوعا وبنو سليم وعبد القيس طوعا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says believers submit willingly and benefit from accepted faith, while unbelievers submit only when they see God's punishment, which then avails them nothing; he cites 40:85.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في الآية قال: أما المؤمن فأسلم طائعا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan specifies the willing submitters as angels in heaven and the Ansar and Abd al-Qays on earth.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن الحسن في الآية قال: في السماء الملائكة طوعا

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Sha'bi explains the submission as God's having subjected them.
rows.anchor: وأخرج عن الشعبي {وله أسلم من في السماوات} قال: استقادتهم له

rows.speaker: أبو سنان
rows.claim: Abu Sinan glosses submission as recognition: anyone asked knows God.
rows.anchor: وأخرج عن أبي سنان {وله أسلم من في السماوات والأرض} قال: المعرفة ليس أحد تسأله إلا عرفه

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima applies unwilling submission to Arab polytheists and captives, including people who entered Islam under compulsion.
rows.anchor: وأخرج عن عكرمة في قوله {وكرها} قال: من أسلم من مشركي العرب والسبايا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Anas reports the Prophet's instruction to recite this verse in the ear of ill-tempered enslaved people, animals, or children.
rows.anchor: عن أنس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: من ساء خلقه من الرقيق

rows.speaker: يونس بن عبيد
rows.claim: Yunus ibn Ubayd says that reciting the verse in the ear of a difficult mount makes it gentle by God's permission.
rows.anchor: عن يونس بن عبيد قال: ليس رجل يكون على دابة صعبة فيقرأ في أذنها

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet describing deeds at Resurrection: prayer, charity, fasting, and then Islam each appear and are told by God that they are good; Islam says God is Peace and it is Islam.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: تجيء الأعمال يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Anas ibn Malik used to apply the prescribed flogging to enslaved women who committed fornication, whether they had married or not.
rows.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك أنه كان يضرب إماءه الحد إذا زنين تزوجن أو لم يتزوجن

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid reports a reading that explicitly includes either male or female offenders: if they commit a sexual offense.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: في بعض القراءة فإن أتوا أو أتين بفاحشة

words: نِصْفُ مَا عَلَى ٱلْمُحْصَنَٰتِ مِنَ ٱلْعَذَابِ
rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud says the enslaved person's half-punishment is fifty lashes, with neither banishment nor stoning.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود في قوله {فعليهن نصف ما على المحصنات من العذاب} قال: خمسون جلدة ولا نفي ولا رجم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas gives forty lashes as the penalty when an enslaved man falsely accuses a free person.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: حد العبد يفتري على الحر أربعون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses al-anat as fornication.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: العنت الزنا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In answer to Nafi ibn al-Azraq, Ibn Abbas also glosses al-anat as sin and cites an Arab poet's line using عنتي for the harm or sin sought against someone.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس إن نافع بن الأزرق سأله عن العنت قال: الإثم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says patient abstention from marrying enslaved women is better.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد {وأن تصبروا خير لكم} قال: عن نكاح الإماء

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud likewise interprets patience as refraining from marrying enslaved women.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود {وأن تصبروا خير لكم} قال: عن نكاح الإماء

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says it is better to refrain from marrying an enslaved woman, although the marriage is lawful, because her children would remain enslaved.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة {وأن تصبروا} عن نكاح الأمة خير وهو حل لكم إسترقاق أولادهن

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says avoiding marriage to an enslaved woman is better so one's children will not be enslaved.
rows.anchor: عن السدي في الآية قال: أن تصبر ولا تنكح الأمة فيكون أولادك مملوكين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas remarks that few men who marry enslaved women escape fornication; Abu Hurayra and Sa'id ibn Jubayr transmit the same saying.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: ما تزحف ناكح الإماء عن الزنا إلا قليلا

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar says that when an enslaved man marries a free woman he has freed half himself, while a free man who marries an enslaved woman has enslaved half himself.
rows.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب قال: إذا نكح العبد الحرة فقد أعتق نصفه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid compares marrying an enslaved woman to eating carrion, blood, or pork: it is permissible only under necessity.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد قال نكاح الأمة كالميتة والدم ولحم الخنزير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says eight verses in al-Nisa are better for this community than all sunrise and sunset; the excerpt names 4:26, 4:27, 4:28, and 4:31 among them.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: ثماني آيات نزلت في سورة النساء

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada recounts that Banu Ubayriq accused the upright Lubayd ibn Sahl of stealing after breaking into Rifa'a ibn Zayd's storeroom; Lubayd confronted them, and Qatada asked the Prophet to recover his uncle's weapons.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: فأتيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقلت: يا رسول الله إن أهل بيت منا أهل جفاء عمدوا إلى عمي

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Banu Ubayriq enlisted Asir ibn Urwa and others to portray the accusation as baseless; the Prophet reproached Qatada, who regretted speaking, then revelation condemned the defense of the traitors and their false accusation of Lubayd.
rows.anchor: فقالوا: يا رسول الله إن قتادة بن النعمان وعمه عمدوا إلى أهل بيت منا أهل إسلام وصلاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account identifies the group who intended to mislead Muhammad as Asir ibn Urwa and his companions, and explains the call to seek forgiveness as concerning what was said to Qatada.
rows.anchor: {واستغفر الله} أي مما قلت لقتادة {إن الله كان غفورا رحيما ولا تجادل عن الذين يختانون أنفسهم}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this account, Ta'ma's allies among the Ansar ask Muhammad to defend him and discredit the Jewish accuser; revelation checks that defense, condemns their private plotting, and exposes Ta'ma, who flees to Mecca and apostatizes.
rows.anchor: من الأنصار فقالوا: يا رسول الله جادل عن طعمة وأكذب اليهودي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account says Ta'ma later tried to steal from his host al-Hajjaj ibn Alaṭ, was expelled, and died after robbing travelers; the verse about opposing the Messenger is applied to him.
rows.anchor: فلما فضح الله طعمة بالقرآن بالمدينة هرب حتى أتى مكة فكفر بعد إسلامه

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says an Ansari entrusted Ta'ma ibn Ubayriq with armor; Ta'ma stole it, blamed the Jew Zayd ibn al-Samin, and enlisted his people to plead before the Prophet, who was inclined to shield him before revelation exposed the lie.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة قال: استودع رجل من الأنصار طعمة بن أبيرق مشربة له فيها درع

words: وَلَا تُجَٰدِلْ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخْتَانُونَ أَنفُسَهُمْ
rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima identifies those who betray themselves as Ta'ma ibn Ubayriq and his people.
rows.anchor: يعني طعمة بن أبيرق وقومه {ها أنتم هؤلاء جادلتم}

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima identifies the innocent man falsely accused as Zayd ibn al-Samin.
rows.anchor: {ثم يرم به بريئا} يعني زيد بن السمين {فقد احتمل بهتانا}

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: In Ikrima's account, the group is Ta'ma's people; the no-good-in-much-secret-talk verse is general, and Ta'ma apostatizes, attempts further thefts, is expelled, and dies stoned after robbing travelers; the account says the verses through 4:116 concern him.
rows.anchor: طعمة بن أبيرق {ولولا فضل الله عليك ورحمته} لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم {لهمت طائفة

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says an Ansari denied keeping entrusted armor; the Prophet initially defended him as apparently innocent after his relatives pleaded, but revelation exposed his betrayal, after which he fled to Mecca and apostatized.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن الضحاك قال: نزلت هذه الآية في رجل من الأنصار استودع درعا فجحدها

words: وَمَن يَكْسِبْ خَطِيٓـَٔةً أَوْ إِثْمًۭا ثُمَّ يَرْمِ بِهِۦ بَرِيٓـًٔا
rows.speaker: عطية العوفي
rows.claim: Atiyya al-Awfi says Ta'ma stole armor, hid it in another man's house, and recruited friends to excuse him before the Prophet; the verse describes his slander of that innocent man.
rows.anchor: عن عطية العوفي أن رجلا يقال له طعمة بن أبيرق سرق درعا

rows.speaker: ناس من الصحابة
rows.claim: A report from some Companions says Adam's children were born as male-female twins who married across birth cohorts; Cain wanted the more beautiful twin born with him, but Adam directed Abel to marry her and Cain refused.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود عن ناس من الصحابة أنه كان لايولد لآدم مولود ألا ولد معه جارية

rows.speaker: ناس من الصحابة
rows.claim: In that report, Adam entrusted his household to heaven, earth, and mountains as he went to Mecca; Cain accepted the trust, then Abel offered a fat yearling while Cain offered grain, and fire consumed Abel's offering alone.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن جرير عن ابن مسعود عن ناس من الصحابة

rows.speaker: ناس من الصحابة
rows.claim: Cain threatened Abel over the marriage; Abel answered that God accepts only from the God-fearing and wanted Cain to bear the sin of killing him together with his own existing sin.
rows.anchor: فغضب وقال: لأقتلنك حتى لا تنكح أختي فقال هابيل {إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says marriage to one's twin sister or another sister was forbidden; after a dispute over a beautiful and an ugly twin, the brothers offered a white ram and grain, God accepted the ram and kept it in Paradise for forty years as Abraham's sacrificial ram, and humanity descends from the unbelieving brother.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: نهى أن ينكح المرأة أخاها توأمها وأن ينكحها غيره من اخوتها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Via al-Dahhak, Ibn Abbas says Adam had forty children, twenty sons and twenty daughters, including the named surviving children; God ordered siblings paired across families in marriage.
rows.anchor: عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس قال: ولد لآدم أربعون ولدا عشرون غلاما وعشرون جارية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says offerings were made before there were poor people to receive charity: a shepherd offered his best sheep and a farmer some crops; fire accepted the sheep, and Cain threatened Abel because people knew whose offering was rejected.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان من شأن ابني آدم أنه لم يكن مسكين يتصدق عليه

words: فَتُقُبِّلَ مِنْ أَحَدِهِمَا وَلَمْ يُتَقَبَّلْ مِنَ ٱلْءَاخَرِ
rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar contrasts the shepherd's best, willingly offered sheep with the farmer's inferior, reluctantly offered crop; God accepted the former, and the murdered brother was stronger but held back by scrupulous fear.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال: إن ابني آدم اللذين قربا قربانا كان أحدهما صاحب حرث

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies the two sons as Habil and Qabil, sons of Adam himself; Abel offered a fine she-goat from his flock, Cain offered crops, and God accepted the sheep, prompting Cain's threat to kill him.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {واتل عليهم نبأ ابني آدم} قال: هابيل وقابيل

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid's account continues: after Cain killed Abel, God bound one of Cain's legs to his thigh; he faced south, endured alternating snow in winter and fire in summer, and was attended by seven angels in rotation.
rows.anchor: فقتله فعقل الله إحدى رجليه بساقه إلى فخذها من يوم قتله إلى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan rejects the view that these were Adam's biological sons: they were Israelites, and the offering story occurred among the Children of Israel; one was the first person to die.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله {واتل عليهم نبأ ابني آدم بالحق} قال: كانا من بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: Abu al-Darda says certainty that God accepted even one prayer would be dearer to him than the whole world.
rows.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء قال: لأن استيقن ان الله

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali says no action is small when accompanied by piety, since what God accepts cannot be considered small.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب قال: لايقل عمل مع تقوى

rows.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
rows.claim: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz writes that God accepts, shows mercy, and rewards only on the basis of piety; preachers of piety are many but practitioners few.
rows.anchor: عن عمر بن عبد العزيز أنه كتب إلى رجل: أوصيك بتقوى الله الذي لايقبل غيرها

rows.speaker: موسى بن أعين
rows.claim: Musa ibn A'yan explains the God-fearing as people who avoid some lawful things lest they fall into what is forbidden.
rows.anchor: سألت موسى بن أعين عن قوله عز وجل

rows.speaker: فضالة بن عبيد
rows.claim: Fadala ibn Ubayd says knowing that God accepted a mustard seed's worth of one's deed would be dearer than the world.
rows.anchor: عن فضالة بن عبيد قال: لأن أكون اعلم أن الله يقبل مني مثقال حبة

rows.speaker: عامر بن عبد قيس
rows.claim: Amir ibn Abd Qays says being made one of the God-fearing, as this verse promises, would be worth more than the whole world.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة قال: قال عامر بن عبد قيس آية في القرآن أحب إلي

rows.speaker: همام بن يحيى
rows.claim: Hammam ibn Yahya recounts that Amir ibn Abdullah wept at death and said he feared the verse that limits acceptance to the God-fearing.
rows.anchor: عن همام بن يحيى قال: بكى عامر بن عبد الله عند الموت

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Al-Hasan transmits that the Prophet said God does not accept a servant's deed until He is pleased with the servant.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله لايقبل عمل عبد

rows.speaker: مطرف
rows.claim: Thabit says Mutarrif would ask God to accept a day's fast and record a good deed, then recite the verse about acceptance and piety.
rows.anchor: عن ثابت قال: كان مطرف يقول: اللهم تقبل مني صيام يوم

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak defines the God-fearing here as those who avoid associating partners with God.
rows.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله {إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين} قال: الذين يتقون الشرك

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar gave a beggar a dinar; when his son prayed for its acceptance, Ibn Umar said certainty about one accepted prostration or dirham would make death more welcome, for God accepts only from the God-fearing.
rows.anchor: عن هشام بن يحيى عن أبيه قال: دخل سائل إلى ابن عمر فقال لابنه: اعطه دينار

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the people addressed had been commanded that if a man wanted to kill another, the victim must let him act and not resist.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {لئن بسطت إلي يدك}

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the Children of Israel were commanded not to resist when one person raised a hand to kill another, but to let the attacker kill or desist.
rows.anchor: عن ابن جريج في الآية قال: كانت بنو إسرائيل كتب عليهم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the brother's sin that Abel wants him to bear is the sin of killing Abel; his own sin is what he had committed beforehand. Qatada and al-Dahhak report the same explanation.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {إني أريد أن تبوء بإثمي وإثمك} قال: بقتلك إياي

words: إِنِّيٓ أُرِيدُ أَن تَبُوٓأَ بِإِثْمِي وَإِثْمِكَ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains tabūʾ as returning with Abel's and the killer's sins and thereby deserving Hell; he supports this Arabic sense with a poet's line using the word باء.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس إن نافع بن الأزرق قال له: أخبرني عن قوله عز وجل {إني أريد أن تبوء بإثمي وإثمك} قال: ترجع

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas reports the Prophet's advice during future civil strife: the seated person is safer than the standing, walking, or running person; if an attacker enters one's home, be like Adam's son. Al-Tirmidhi grades it good and al-Hakim authenticates it.
rows.anchor: عن سعد بن أبي وقاص: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: إنها ستكون فتنة
